correctness.rationale: The proof derives turning-angle period m by comparing the two Tabachnikov isosceles trapezoids indexed i and i+m. This forces opposite edge vectors and central symmetry. Equal side and (m-1)-diagonal lengths then give a constant adjacent sum of squared radii via the parallelogram identity, hence 2-periodicity. For odd m, central symmetry swaps the two parity classes, forcing a single circumradius; strict convexity makes equal chords have equal central angles, hence regularity. For even m, the cited construction supplies nonregular examples.
risks: The theorem is stated for strict convexity; degenerate convex boundary cases are intentionally not claimed.

value.rationale: The parameter line k=n/2-1 is natural and adjacent to the half-diagonal regime in the published global classification problem. The result is not a small numerical increment: it supplies a uniform structural theorem for every member of the line and a complete parity classification, with infinitely many new rigid cases and a sharp flexible complement already witnessed by prior constructions.
